title: Cashiering Clearing Q&A: Uncleared Check Payments at an Electric Service by Rate Schedule Restore
content:
These answers set out when recent check payments on an idle Electric Service by Rate Schedule account are added back to the restore payment because they have not cleared.

**The account has a returned payment dated less than twelve whole months before the current date. What is added back?** Every online e-check payment and every office check payment dated less than one whole month before the current date.

**No returned payment is dated in those twelve months. What is added back?** For each of the two channels — online e-check and office check — the latest payment through that channel, when it is dated no more than 5 calendar days before the current date.

**And otherwise?** Nothing is added back; the balance is taken with every payment as posted.

The amount added back is added to the restore payment before that payment is rounded to the cent and held at no less than zero.

### Hypothetical case (current date April 20)

Payments: online e-check $60.00 on April 2; office check $80.00 on April 17; mailed check $50.00 on April 18.

| Returned payment in the twelve months | Added back |
|---|---|
| Yes | $60.00 and $80.00, $140.00 — the mailed check is not an online e-check or office check |
| No | $80.00 — the office check is 3 days old; the e-check of April 2 is the latest e-check and is 18 days old |

### Point of reading

- A payment dated exactly 5 calendar days before the current date is within the clearing period; one dated 6 days before is not.
